pathway.title: Ferrellgas Partners L P — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: The business profile is adequate: scale and customer stickiness support cash-flow visibility, but weather decides the volume. The company is the second-largest US retail marketer with a national footprint, about 70% of its residential customers use company-owned tanks, and 56% of propane volume is sold in the five winter months, so a warm winter cut volumes by 3.13% and revenue by 3.83% in fiscal 2026. Basis: calculation C01; calculation C09; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 62

Margins are the main support. Adjusted EBITDA fell only 2.84% on the 3.83% revenue fall, and its margin stayed within 0.22 percentage points over three years, at 17.24% in fiscal 2026, because cost of sales fell faster than revenue. This rests on the issuer's own add-backs: reported EBITDA of fiscal 2025 was only 58.15% of adjusted EBITDA, mostly because of legal charges, so the stable margin is an adjusted view. Basis: calculation C01; calculation C16; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 59–61; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 167–168

Free cash flow is the weakest dimension. Conversion of adjusted EBITDA into free cash flow fell from 55.05% in fiscal 2024 to 17.04% and 23.45% in the next two years as cash interest paid rose 41.85% and capital expenditure took 24.06% of adjusted EBITDA. Preferred distributions took 87.24% of the year's free cash flow, and with the final Class B payout the distributions were 229.27% of it. Basis: calculation C03; calculation C04; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 118; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Leverage is moderate and has drifted up while cover weakened. Total debt is 4.81x adjusted EBITDA against 4.44x a year earlier, and 5.07x reported EBITDA, with debt up 5.29%. The October 2025 refinancing replaced the 2026 notes with higher-coupon 2031 notes, and the fixed-rate notes are 94.20% of principal, so the rate risk is the coupon already set rather than future rate moves. Basis: calculation C02; calculation C08; calculation C13; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 142–146; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Liquidity is adequate but seasonal and facility-dependent. At year end liquidity was USD 195.1 million, USD 64.6 million lower than a year earlier, and availability equalled the revolver commitment less borrowings and letters of credit, so the commitment and not the borrowing base was binding at that date. A further USD 20.0 million was drawn on August 27, 2026, and the borrowing base falls with receivables and inventory in a weak winter. Basis: calculation C06; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 143–144; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 147–148; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 64

Refinancing capacity rests on a narrow window. The revolver matures in October 2028 and the 2029 notes in April 2029, which together are 58.27% of principal, the rating agencies reversed their 2025 downgrades in October 2025, and market access was shown by the 2025 refinancing, but at a coupon 387.5 bp higher. The preferred distribution rate steps up toward its cap and the preferred holders gain a forced-sale path from March 2031, so each refinancing competes with a rising senior equity claim. Basis: calculation C07; calculation C08; calculation C12; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 143–149; 10-K_2025-07-31_fgpr-20250731.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-Q_2026-01-31_fgpr-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 61

Governance and financial policy are a medium risk. Business & governance finds control with a general partner owned by an employee trust, no payouts to Class A holders in two years, cash-paid preferred units and a majority of independent directors, but also the removal of the six-times Class B payout rule in March 2026 and a final Class B payout that exceeded free cash flow. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C04

On the fiscal 2026 base, adjusted EBITDA less capital expenditures covers the notes' coupons plus the preferred cash cost 1.38x, falling to 1.31x at the preferred cap. That leaves a thin amount for the revolver, leases, taxes and working capital before any debt reduction, which is why a second year of weak volume matters more than the headline leverage. Basis: calculation C05; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 74; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 149–150

759.571 million gallons sold, down 3.13%: retail 556.207 million gallons, down 1.89%, and wholesale 203.364 million gallons, down 6.36%
USD 1,023.953 million, 54.93% of revenue, against 52.77% in fiscal 2025; margin is the cents-per-gallon spread over delivered propane cost

3,934 full-time employees of the general partner, 3,560 in field operations and 374 in corporate functions; less than 1% are union members
Capital expenditures of USD 77.315 million in fiscal 2026, of which maintenance capital expenditures were USD 28.006 million

runs.text: Strength, scale and customer stickiness: the second-largest US retail propane marketer runs a national network of distribution locations, and about 70% of residential customers use company-owned tanks that only the owning supplier may fill in some states. That scale spreads delivery and procurement cost and the tank ownership keeps volume sticky, which supports cash-flow visibility for debt service. Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 15

Strength, margin resilience: adjusted EBITDA fell 2.84% on a 3.83% revenue fall and its margin held between 17.06% and 17.28% over three years, because cost of sales fell faster than revenue. This shows the cost base and pricing spread absorb a mild volume loss, which protects interest cover in a warm year. Basis: calculation C01; calculation C16; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 60–62

Strength, refinancing completed with ratings restored: the 2026 notes were redeemed in October 2025 and Moody's and S&P reversed their 2025 downgrades, lifting the corporate rating to B2. This removed the nearest senior maturity and gives about two years before the revolver falls due, which buys time to rebuild cover. Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 143–145; 10-K_2025-07-31_fgpr-20250731.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-Q_2026-01-31_fgpr-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 61

Strength, a cash-paid preferred and no Class A payouts: preferred distributions are paid in cash, so the claim does not compound, and no cash went to Class A holders or the general partner in fiscal 2025 or 2026. This keeps equity leakage to contractual payouts only. Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 149–150; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 154

Strength, modest maintenance spending: maintenance capital expenditure was 36.22% of the total, so some spending can be deferred in stress. This is a lever that is not confirmed by the filing, since the rest of the spending is not described as discretionary. Basis: calculation C15; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 60

Weakness, weather exposure: 56% of propane volume sells in the five winter months and the fourth quarter gave only 7.39% of adjusted EBITDA, so one warm winter cuts the year's earnings while fixed delivery and interest costs continue. This is the first break in the downside path. Basis: calculation C09; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 62

Weakness, thin free cash flow after fixed claims: free cash flow converted 23.45% of adjusted EBITDA in fiscal 2026 and preferred distributions took 87.24% of it. Little is left to repay debt, so leverage falls only if earnings grow. Basis: calculation C03; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 118

Weakness, higher and rising fixed charges: the 2031 notes carry a coupon 387.5 bp above the 2026 notes they replaced, and the preferred distribution rate steps up by 216.9 bp to its cap. Cash interest has risen and adjusted cover has fallen from 3.56x to 2.54x, and the preferred steps add to the claims ahead of equity. Basis: calculation C08; calculation C12; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 145–149

Weakness, concentrated maturities: the revolver and the 2029 notes together are USD 912.5 million, 58.27% of principal, due between October 2028 and April 2029. Refinancing both inside six months in a weak winter would be costly. Basis: calculation C07; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 143–147

Weakness, payouts and control: the general partner controls the issuer, and the final Class B payout and preferred distributions exceeded free cash flow in fiscal 2026. The removal of the six-times payout rule leaves only contract limits on later Class A payouts. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C04

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The only new debt issue in the supplied period is the senior unsecured notes due 2031. On October 27, 2025 the operating partnership and its finance subsidiary issued USD 650.0 million of 9.25% notes at par and used net proceeds of about USD 637.5 million, with cash on hand, to redeem all USD 650.0 million of the 2026 notes. The 2031 notes mature on January 15, 2031, are guaranteed by the general partner and by domestic subsidiaries other than the named exclusions, and may be redeemed before January 15, 2028 at par plus a make-whole premium, or in part from equity offerings at a premium. On the same day the credit agreement was amended to extend its maturity to October 27, 2028 and to raise the maximum commitment to USD 350.0 million, subject to a borrowing base, with an accordion of USD 50.0 million. Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 143; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 145–146

The refinancing lengthened the maturity profile at a higher coupon and raised the secured revolver commitment from USD 308.8 million to USD 350.0 million. The extra coupon is sized in Financial foundation. The credit facility now matures in 2028, before the 2029 notes, so the revolver comes up for refinancing first. Basis: calculation C13; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 143–146

The equity-side transactions of fiscal 2026 were a final Class B distribution of USD 107.0 million paid on March 13, 2026, the conversion of all Class B units into Class A units on March 16, 2026 at the lower conversion factor, and the expiry of the 20% voting cap on Class A units on March 30, 2026. The Class A unit count rose only through that conversion, so no equity was sold for cash, and no contribution by the owner is disclosed. Basis: calculation C05; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 153–154

After year end the operating partnership borrowed a further USD 20.0 million under the credit facility on August 27, 2026 at 7.0% for working capital, which lifts short-term borrowings from USD 87.5 million at year end to USD 107.5 million before any repayment. The filing states no other subsequent event, and none of the fiscal 2026 cash flow shows an acquisition. Basis: calculation C13; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 143; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 168; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 118

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reported leverage looks better than it is. Total debt at the July 2026 year end is 5.07x reported EBITDA and net debt 4.91x, against 7.63x and 7.13x a year earlier, but the FY2025 base carried USD 130.635 million of legal fees and settlements outside the core business. On the issuer's adjusted EBITDA, which removes that charge, total debt rose from 4.44x to 4.81x because carrying debt grew by USD 77.599 million while adjusted EBITDA fell by USD 9.388 million. On reported EBITDA the FY2024 level of 4.76x is the cleaner comparison, and FY2026 sits above it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash interest cover is the weaker side. Cash interest paid rose to USD 126.465 million from USD 96.072 million, so reported EBITDA covers it 2.41x against 2.00x in FY2025 and 3.45x in FY2024. The October 2025 refinancing replaced USD 650.000 million of senior notes due 2026 with senior notes due 2031 at a much higher coupon; at the stated coupons that principal alone costs USD 25.1875 million more a year, and the two senior note issues together carry USD 108.594 million of coupons in fiscal 2027, the amount the issuer's own table of fixed-rate interest obligations shows, before the revolver, lease interest and fees. The new notes were outstanding for about nine of the twelve months of fiscal 2026, so a full year of the higher coupon is not yet in the fiscal 2026 figures. The last-twelve-months cover of 3.64x at April 30, 2026 is not comparable with fiscal years because that period excludes the first payment on the new notes.

fields.value: Cash generation covers the preferred units but not the Class B distribution. Operating cash flow of USD 152.660 million less capital expenditures of USD 77.315 million leaves free cash flow of USD 75.345 million, against USD 56.345 million in FY2025 and USD 174.714 million in FY2024. Cash distributions to the senior preferred units took USD 65.729 million, leaving USD 9.616 million, and the USD 107.016 million Class B distribution in March 2026 turned free cash flow after both distributions negative at USD 97.400 million; the revolver was drawn by USD 87.500 million in the same year and cash fell by USD 48.461 million. Operating cash flow was also held down by a USD 47.635 million outflow in other current liabilities; the note on that line shows accrued payroll falling from USD 31.072 million to USD 7.307 million and accrued miscellaneous items from USD 47.578 million to USD 10.988 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is thinner than a year ago and depends on a borrowing base. Cash of USD 48.422 million and stated facility availability of USD 146.7 million give USD 195.1 million at July 31, 2026, against USD 259.7 million at July 31, 2025 and USD 219.7 million at April 30, 2026. Availability is the lesser of the USD 350.0 million commitment and a borrowing base of USD 250.0 million plus 80% of eligible receivables and 70% of eligible propane inventory, less borrowings and letters of credit of USD 115.8 million. A further USD 20.0 million was drawn on August 27, 2026, which leaves net debt unchanged at drawdown but uses availability. Scheduled principal of USD 1.310 million is due in fiscal 2027, the revolver matures on October 27, 2028, and the first large maturity is USD 825.550 million in fiscal 2029, followed by USD 650.200 million in fiscal 2031.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A non-debt funding float and several claims sit outside debt. Deferred revenue under even-pay billing was USD 41.232 million at July 31, 2026, down from USD 43.490 million and USD 50.175 million in the two prior years, so customer prepayments fund less of working capital each year. Finance lease liabilities of USD 56.089 million, operating lease liabilities of USD 37.861 million, a pension withdrawal liability of USD 3.380 million in payments and product purchase commitments of USD 39.927 million are excluded from Total Debt; adding the finance leases alone would lift total debt to 5.26x reported EBITDA. The senior preferred units carry USD 651.349 million in mezzanine equity and accrued distributions of USD 65.231 million a year, which rank ahead of equity but are in no ratio here.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The downside chain starts with weather and volumes. Propane volumes fell 3% in FY2026 and revenues fell 3.83%; a warm winter cuts volumes in the second and third fiscal quarters, which carry most of the year's operating profit, and the delivery and personnel cost base then compresses EBITDA while interest cost is already higher. With reported cover at 2.41x, the first observable stress is cash interest cover and revolver usage, followed by borrowing-base availability, because receivables and inventory fall when volumes fall. The filing prints covenant levels but no covenant ratio or headroom, so headroom is not calculated here.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest contrary evidence is that adjusted EBITDA fell only 2.84% on a 3.83% revenue decline, no senior maturity falls before fiscal 2029, and the filing states compliance with all debt covenants at year end. A fall in revolver borrowings, a return to the FY2024 cover level of 3.45x and continued cash generation after preferred distributions would change the view.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business and governance for Ferrellgas Partners L P (fgpr-922358), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the business, ownership, control, related-party and sponsor-behaviour facts in the four supplied filings, with the transactions that shaped the capital structure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No external sources were used. The run settings are not issuer evidence and are not listed as a source.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Creditor governance risk is medium: the general partner is controlled by an employee-owned parent, and fiscal 2026 preferred and Class B distributions equalled 229.27% of free cash flow, while the March 2026 Class B conversion removed a brake on Class A payouts.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C07; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 154; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The risk is not high because no cash went to Class A unitholders or the general partner in fiscal 2025 or fiscal 2026, the preferred units are paid in cash rather than in kind, the general partner takes no management fee and seven of nine directors are independent. It is not low because the preferred holders may gain a right to force a sale from March 2031, the partnership agreements remove default fiduciary duties, and the executed debt documents that set what may be paid out were not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Control rests with the general partner, not with unitholders, and the owner holds a small share of the units. Ferrellgas, Inc. manages both partnerships, is wholly owned by Ferrell Companies, and that parent is owned 100% by an employee stock ownership trust whose independent trustee votes the shares. Ferrell Companies and its affiliates beneficially own 10.03% of the Class A units, and the Chairman of the board holds a further 2.23%, so creditors cannot count on unitholder votes to restrain the general partner.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C04; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 103–105; 10-Q_2026-01-31_fgpr-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The preferred units are the real counterweight and also the largest claim ahead of the equity. The USD 700.0 million issue carries a cash distribution rate that steps up each year to a cap, so at the stated rates the annual cash cost rises by 216.9 bp of the issue between the original rate and the cap, which would take it from 19.51% to 24.24% of fiscal 2026 adjusted EBITDA. The holders have a board seat, consent rights over change of control, indebtedness and similar actions, and from March 2031 a path to a forced sale of the operating partnership if more than a third of the units are still outstanding and are not redeemed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Payouts to holders ranking below creditors were large in fiscal 2026 and were not fully covered by cash generation. Preferred distributions of USD 65.7 million and the final Class B distribution of USD 107.0 million together were 229.27% of free cash flow. The operating partnership, which is the borrower, paid the USD 107.0 million up to Ferrellgas Partners on March 6, 2026 and Ferrellgas Partners paid it to Class B holders a week later. The revolver was drawn by USD 87.5 million in the same year, which the issuer attributes to refinancing and litigation settlement costs, and the filing does not say how the Class B payment was funded.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C05; calculation C07; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 150–154; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 69; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 73; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 118; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The Class B conversion reduced control risk but also removed a constraint on Class A payouts. Class B holders had received cash equal to the USD 357.0 million principal of the notes they exchanged in 2021, and on March 16, 2026 their units converted into Class A units at the lower conversion factor, 15 days before it rose, and the units issued equal 57.23% of the Class A units now outstanding. The conversion ended their contingent right to acquire the general partner interests and ended a rule that required Class B holders to receive six times any payout to Class A holders or the general partner, which had made such payouts costly.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C04; calculation C05; 10-K_2025-07-31_fgpr-20250731.htm.jsonl, pages 155–156; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 153–154; 10-Q_2026-01-31_fgpr-20260131.htm.jsonl, pages 27–28

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Payouts to Class A holders and the general partner are now limited by contract, and the contracts were not supplied. The Ferrellgas Partners agreement requires quarterly distribution of all available cash within 45 days of quarter end, and that cash depends on what the operating partnership may pay up under net leverage and liquidity tests in the credit agreement, both note indentures and the preferred-unit terms. No Class A or general partner distribution was paid in fiscal 2025 or 2026. Capacity and willingness are separate questions: the tests are described but cannot be worked, and the absence of payouts was also the result of the six-times rule, so it is weak evidence of restraint.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Related-party leakage is small, but the cost base itself runs through the general partner. The partnership has no employees, and reimbursement of the general partner's costs of USD 347.7 million was 49.98% of operating and administrative expense in fiscal 2026. The general partner takes no management fee, and the disclosed payments to directors' firms were USD 1.2 million for refinancing advice and USD 0.8 million for legal services, against USD 3.0 million of legal fees a year earlier.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C08; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 95; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 105–106; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 163

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The board is mostly independent and reporting is conventional, but board and finance leadership changed within the year. Seven of nine directors are independent and the audit committee is made up of independent financial experts; two directors joined in 2026, one of them a paid adviser who is not counted as independent, and the director designated by Class B holders was removed after conversion. No chief financial officer is listed: the principal financial officer is the Vice President and Corporate Controller.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C12; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 83–93; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 103–106; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 81

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business is the second-largest US retail propane marketer, with earnings driven by weather rather than by customer concentration. Retail sales were 64.64% of fiscal 2026 revenue and wholesale, mainly portable tank exchange and bulk sales to resellers, 28.78%. A winter 11% warmer than the year before cut volumes by 3.13%, while gross margin rose to 54.93% of revenue from 52.77%, and the fourth quarter contributed only 7.39% of fiscal 2026 adjusted EBITDA, which leaves the winter quarters decisive.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C03; calculation C10; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 8–11; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 60–62; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The history explains why the structure looks as it does. The 2021 restructuring converted USD 357.0 million of Ferrellgas Partners notes into Class B units and created USD 700.0 million of preferred units, and the 2017 Eddystone lawsuit was settled in January 2025 for USD 125.0 million, paid in three instalments to January 2026, which released a USD 190.0 million appeal bond. Bridger Logistics, a named defendant, remains outside the guarantee group for the credit facility and both note series.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence for a lower risk rating is conduct: no distribution went to Class A holders or the general partner for three years apart from USD 1.0 million to the general partner in fiscal 2024, the preferred units have been paid in cash, the general partner takes no management fee, no loans to management are disclosed, the October 2025 refinancing replaced the 2026 notes with senior unsecured notes on the same guarantee terms as the 2029 notes, and the one legacy lawsuit has been settled and paid. Moody's and S&P reversed their 2025 downgrades in October 2025, lifting the corporate rating from B3 to B2. Disclosure controls were effective, the audit report has no critical audit matters, and the Class B conversion removed the holders' option to take over the general partner.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would move to low if the executed documents showed tight payout baskets and the preferred holders' consent rights held firm while leverage fell, and if no Class A or general partner payout were made after conversion. It would move to high if Class A or general partner distributions resumed while the revolver was drawn, if the preferred units were paid in kind, if fees or transactions with directors' firms grew, or if the holders prepared to use the 2031 sale right before the 2029 and 2031 notes were refinanced.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The executed indentures, credit agreement and partnership agreements were not supplied, so every statement about what may be paid out rests on the issuer's own summaries; if the baskets prove wider than described, the medium risk level should rise.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The identity and current holdings of the preferred and former Class B holders are not disclosed beyond one 2021 purchase of USD 246.0 million, so who can act as the required holders, and whether control of the preferred consent rights is concentrated, is not established; this could move the 2031 sale-right assessment either way.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The funding source of the March 2026 Class B distribution is not stated, and the issuer ties the revolver draw to other costs, so the finding that cash generation did not cover it rests on the arithmetic of free cash flow, not on a disclosed link.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Rating actions are known only from the issuer's own description at month precision, and no agency report, outlook or market price was supplied, so rating pressure from the ownership structure cannot be assessed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The preferred redemption amount depends on distributions paid since 2021, of which only three fiscal years are supplied, so the cost of redeeming the preferred units is not calculable and the size of the 2031 event cannot be stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The only new debt issue in the supplied period is the senior unsecured notes due 2031. On October 27, 2025 the operating partnership and its finance subsidiary issued USD 650.0 million of 9.25% notes at par and used net proceeds of about USD 637.5 million, with cash on hand, to redeem all USD 650.0 million of the 2026 notes. The 2031 notes mature on January 15, 2031, are guaranteed by the general partner and by domestic subsidiaries other than the named exclusions, and may be redeemed before January 15, 2028 at par plus a make-whole premium, or in part from equity offerings at a premium. On the same day the credit agreement was amended to extend its maturity to October 27, 2028 and to raise the maximum commitment to USD 350.0 million, subject to a borrowing base, with an accordion of USD 50.0 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The refinancing lengthened the maturity profile at a higher coupon and raised the secured revolver commitment from USD 308.8 million to USD 350.0 million. The extra coupon is sized in Financial foundation. The credit facility now matures in 2028, before the 2029 notes, so the revolver comes up for refinancing first.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C13; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 143–146

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The equity-side transactions of fiscal 2026 were a final Class B distribution of USD 107.0 million paid on March 13, 2026, the conversion of all Class B units into Class A units on March 16, 2026 at the lower conversion factor, and the expiry of the 20% voting cap on Class A units on March 30, 2026. The Class A unit count rose only through that conversion, so no equity was sold for cash, and no contribution by the owner is disclosed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: After year end the operating partnership borrowed a further USD 20.0 million under the credit facility on August 27, 2026 at 7.0% for working capital, which lifts short-term borrowings from USD 87.5 million at year end to USD 107.5 million before any repayment. The filing states no other subsequent event, and none of the fiscal 2026 cash flow shows an acquisition.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit for Ferrellgas Partners L P (fgpr-922358), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is one integrated credit view of the business, cash flow, liquidity, refinancing capacity and governance, built from the four supplied filings and the three earlier analyses.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No external sources were used. The run settings are not issuer evidence and are not listed as a source.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit quality is constrained: a scale propane distributor earns about USD 321.3 million of adjusted EBITDA, but leverage of 4.81x, interest cover of 2.54x and preferred payouts that absorb 87.24% of free cash flow leave little room for a warm winter.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C02; calculation C03; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 64

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business profile is adequate, with the second-largest US retail propane position, tank-owning customers and margins that held in fiscal 2026. The financial profile is weak: cash interest cover fell from 3.56x to 2.54x, liquidity was USD 195.1 million against USD 259.7 million a year earlier, and USD 912.5 million of revolver and note maturities fall between October 2028 and April 2029.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C06; calculation C07; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 64

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business profile is adequate: scale and customer stickiness support cash-flow visibility, but weather decides the volume. The company is the second-largest US retail marketer with a national footprint, about 70% of its residential customers use company-owned tanks, and 56% of propane volume is sold in the five winter months, so a warm winter cut volumes by 3.13% and revenue by 3.83% in fiscal 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C01; calculation C09; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 62

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins are the main support. Adjusted EBITDA fell only 2.84% on the 3.83% revenue fall, and its margin stayed within 0.22 percentage points over three years, at 17.24% in fiscal 2026, because cost of sales fell faster than revenue. This rests on the issuer's own add-backs: reported EBITDA of fiscal 2025 was only 58.15% of adjusted EBITDA, mostly because of legal charges, so the stable margin is an adjusted view.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C01; calculation C16; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 59–61; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 167–168

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Free cash flow is the weakest dimension. Conversion of adjusted EBITDA into free cash flow fell from 55.05% in fiscal 2024 to 17.04% and 23.45% in the next two years as cash interest paid rose 41.85% and capital expenditure took 24.06% of adjusted EBITDA. Preferred distributions took 87.24% of the year's free cash flow, and with the final Class B payout the distributions were 229.27% of it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C03; calculation C04; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 118; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage is moderate and has drifted up while cover weakened. Total debt is 4.81x adjusted EBITDA against 4.44x a year earlier, and 5.07x reported EBITDA, with debt up 5.29%. The October 2025 refinancing replaced the 2026 notes with higher-coupon 2031 notes, and the fixed-rate notes are 94.20% of principal, so the rate risk is the coupon already set rather than future rate moves.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C02; calculation C08; calculation C13; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 142–146; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is adequate but seasonal and facility-dependent. At year end liquidity was USD 195.1 million, USD 64.6 million lower than a year earlier, and availability equalled the revolver commitment less borrowings and letters of credit, so the commitment and not the borrowing base was binding at that date. A further USD 20.0 million was drawn on August 27, 2026, and the borrowing base falls with receivables and inventory in a weak winter.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C06; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 143–144; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 147–148; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 64

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Refinancing capacity rests on a narrow window. The revolver matures in October 2028 and the 2029 notes in April 2029, which together are 58.27% of principal, the rating agencies reversed their 2025 downgrades in October 2025, and market access was shown by the 2025 refinancing, but at a coupon 387.5 bp higher. The preferred distribution rate steps up toward its cap and the preferred holders gain a forced-sale path from March 2031, so each refinancing competes with a rising senior equity claim.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C07; calculation C08; calculation C12; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 143–149; 10-K_2025-07-31_fgpr-20250731.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-Q_2026-01-31_fgpr-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 61

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Governance and financial policy are a medium risk. Business & governance finds control with a general partner owned by an employee trust, no payouts to Class A holders in two years, cash-paid preferred units and a majority of independent directors, but also the removal of the six-times Class B payout rule in March 2026 and a final Class B payout that exceeded free cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: On the fiscal 2026 base, adjusted EBITDA less capital expenditures covers the notes' coupons plus the preferred cash cost 1.38x, falling to 1.31x at the preferred cap. That leaves a thin amount for the revolver, leases, taxes and working capital before any debt reduction, which is why a second year of weak volume matters more than the headline leverage.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence for a better view is resilience. Adjusted EBITDA fell less than revenue in a winter 11% warmer than the year before, no senior notes mature before April 2029, the issuer refinanced USD 650.0 million of 2026 notes in October 2025 and regained a B2 corporate rating, distributions to Class A holders and the general partner were nil, and the issuer states that cash flow, cash and the revolver are sufficient for the foreseeable future, which is management language and not independent evidence.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C01; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 62–65; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 143–145; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 154; 10-Q_2026-01-31_fgpr-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 61; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would improve if a normal or cold winter restored cover toward the fiscal 2024 level of 3.56x, if the revolver were extended well before October 2028, and if free cash flow after preferred distributions were positive without a revolver draw. It would worsen if cover on the cash-paid basis, 2.54x, or on the issuer's net cash interest basis, 2.79x, fell below the 2.50x level of the credit agreement test, whose definition is not supplied, if summer revolver use rose from the USD 87.5 million of year end, or if the revolver were not extended ahead of October 2028 and the 2029 notes were not addressed in the months after.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C02; calculation C06; calculation C11; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 64–65; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 143–145; 10-Q_2026-01-31_fgpr-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 61

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The credit agreement and indenture definitions and the issuer's own covenant ratios are not supplied, so the cover and leverage ratios here are proxies; if the defined ratios differ materially, the liquidity and refinancing assessments could be too mild or too severe.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No peer set, market price or agency report was supplied, so the adequate business profile and weak financial profile are absolute judgements and not rankings against other leveraged propane or energy-distribution issuers.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No management forecast or guidance for fiscal 2027 is supplied, so the outlook and the downside path rest on the fiscal 2026 pattern and on stated contractual dates, and a different winter could change both.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The first-quarter fiscal 2026 report is not supplied, so the lowest liquidity point of the year is not measured and the claim that the revolver bridges the summer rests on the year-end and April balances.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Margin resilience is shown on the issuer's adjusted EBITDA, which excludes large legal items and adds back legal costs of the core business; on reported EBITDA the fiscal 2025 margin collapses, so the margin finding is weaker if the add-backs are rejected.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength, scale and customer stickiness: the second-largest US retail propane marketer runs a national network of distribution locations, and about 70% of residential customers use company-owned tanks that only the owning supplier may fill in some states. That scale spreads delivery and procurement cost and the tank ownership keeps volume sticky, which supports cash-flow visibility for debt service.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength, margin resilience: adjusted EBITDA fell 2.84% on a 3.83% revenue fall and its margin held between 17.06% and 17.28% over three years, because cost of sales fell faster than revenue. This shows the cost base and pricing spread absorb a mild volume loss, which protects interest cover in a warm year.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C01; calculation C16; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 60–62

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength, refinancing completed with ratings restored: the 2026 notes were redeemed in October 2025 and Moody's and S&P reversed their 2025 downgrades, lifting the corporate rating to B2. This removed the nearest senior maturity and gives about two years before the revolver falls due, which buys time to rebuild cover.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength, a cash-paid preferred and no Class A payouts: preferred distributions are paid in cash, so the claim does not compound, and no cash went to Class A holders or the general partner in fiscal 2025 or 2026. This keeps equity leakage to contractual payouts only.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength, modest maintenance spending: maintenance capital expenditure was 36.22% of the total, so some spending can be deferred in stress. This is a lever that is not confirmed by the filing, since the rest of the spending is not described as discretionary.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness, weather exposure: 56% of propane volume sells in the five winter months and the fourth quarter gave only 7.39% of adjusted EBITDA, so one warm winter cuts the year's earnings while fixed delivery and interest costs continue. This is the first break in the downside path.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness, thin free cash flow after fixed claims: free cash flow converted 23.45% of adjusted EBITDA in fiscal 2026 and preferred distributions took 87.24% of it. Little is left to repay debt, so leverage falls only if earnings grow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness, higher and rising fixed charges: the 2031 notes carry a coupon 387.5 bp above the 2026 notes they replaced, and the preferred distribution rate steps up by 216.9 bp to its cap. Cash interest has risen and adjusted cover has fallen from 3.56x to 2.54x, and the preferred steps add to the claims ahead of equity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C08; calculation C12; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 145–149

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness, concentrated maturities: the revolver and the 2029 notes together are USD 912.5 million, 58.27% of principal, due between October 2028 and April 2029. Refinancing both inside six months in a weak winter would be costly.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness, payouts and control: the general partner controls the issuer, and the final Class B payout and preferred distributions exceeded free cash flow in fiscal 2026. The removal of the six-times payout rule leaves only contract limits on later Class A payouts.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ferrellgas Partners is a holding partnership whose operating partnership sells propane and related equipment to residential, industrial/commercial, agricultural, portable tank exchange and wholesale customers in all 50 states, the District of Columbia and Puerto Rico. Retail sales were 64.64% of fiscal 2026 revenue and wholesale sales, mainly tank exchange and bulk sales to resellers, 28.78%. Customers are billed on delivery with payment due in about 30 days, and residential customers can spread annual heating cost over twelve months, so revenue is earned as gallons are delivered rather than under long contracts.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The model supports cash-flow visibility only in part. Tank ownership by the company keeps residential volume with the supplier, and the national tank exchange network adds counter-seasonal summer volume, but volume per customer follows the weather and the filing gives no contract duration, renewal rate or customer concentration measure. For creditors the business gives steady demand for a necessity fuel but not a contracted revenue stream, so debt service depends on a normal winter, and refinancing confidence depends on cover holding up through one.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ferrellgas Partners owns about 99.0% of the operating partnership apart from the preferred units, and the operating partnership is the borrower and the main asset holder. The general partner, Ferrellgas, Inc., is owned by Ferrell Companies, which an employee stock ownership trust owns in full, and the preferred units rank ahead of every other equity claim in the operating partnership. Business & governance concludes that creditor governance risk is medium, with control by the general partner, nil payouts to Class A holders and a final Class B payout that exceeded free cash flow in fiscal 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 143–146; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 151

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: For creditors the structural point is that the notes and the revolver sit at the operating partnership, which is also where preferred distributions and payouts to Ferrellgas Partners are paid from, so cash can leave the borrower to the holding partnership and preferred holders on the contract terms rather than on creditor approval. The executed documents that set these terms were not supplied, so the structural conclusion rests on the issuer's summaries.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Volume is the driver and weather decides it: 56% of propane volume sells in the five winter months, volumes fell 3.13% in fiscal 2026 and revenue fell 3.83%, and a wholesale propane price 9% lower also cut revenue per gallon. Price per gallon is a spread over delivered cost, so pass-through of cost changes is the pricing mechanism; contracted-price commitments are hedged with derivatives, and a sudden price rise that is not hedged would compress margin. Revenue is cyclical with weather, not discretionary, and not shown to be concentrated, though no concentration measure is disclosed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C01; calculation C09; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 24–25; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 56; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 62

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The credit link is that revenue is predictable in structure but not in amount: a repeat of the fiscal 2026 volume fall would cut revenue by a similar rate, and a colder winter would lift it. Switching costs from rented tanks make the base sticky, which limits loss of customers, but they do not protect volume per customer.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Personnel is 53.98% of operating expense, vehicles 17.84% and plant and other 28.18%, and operating plus general expense is 37.32% of revenue, so most cost is people and delivery assets that do not fall with volume. Operating leverage is therefore real, yet adjusted EBITDA fell only 2.84% in fiscal 2026 because cost of sales fell 8.24% against the 3.83% fall in revenue, and management states that converting Will Call locations to automatic fill improved routing and margin. Labour and fuel are the cost risks: fuel cost rose in fiscal 2026 and the issuer warns of rising labour cost that may not be recovered in price.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C10; calculation C16; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 25–26; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 62–63; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 167–168

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins can be defended under a mild volume fall but not under a combined shock of lower volume and labour inflation, because the fixed share of cost is large and the add-backs behind adjusted EBITDA are the issuer's own. The credit link is that cover holds only while cost control continues to offset volume.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital expenditure was 24.06% of adjusted EBITDA in fiscal 2026, of which 36.22% was maintenance, and working capital is seasonal: receivables were 40.13% higher at April 30, 2026 than at the prior year end before collection. Cash taxes are small because the partnership passes income through, cash interest and the preferred distributions are the large claims, and finance leases add principal payments outside the debt figure. Free cash flow converted 23.45% of adjusted EBITDA in fiscal 2026 against 55.05% in fiscal 2024.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C03; calculation C14; calculation C15; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 118; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 60; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 155–156; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 164

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The credit link is that EBITDA does not translate into durable free cash flow for deleveraging: after the preferred distributions only a small margin remains, and capital expenditure flexibility over the 2028–2029 maturity wall is limited to the maintenance share and to growth spending the filing does not describe.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C03; calculation C05; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 143–147

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Competitive rivalry is moderate: most retail locations compete with three or more marketers on reliability, safety and price, and competition comes from large multi-state marketers and small local ones, so the second-largest scale position helps cost but does not remove price competition. The credit link is that rivalry limits the spread per gallon and any price recovery after cost inflation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The threat of new entrants is low to moderate because a national tank exchange network and technology platform need scale, and a local entrant faces the cost of tank and truck assets, but local entry into a single market is possible. The threat of substitutes is moderate: propane competes with natural gas, electricity and fuel oil, supplies about 1% of US energy, and is displaced where natural gas pipelines extend, which erodes volume slowly rather than quickly. Buyer power is low for residential customers with rented tanks and higher for large tank exchange retailers, whose concentration is not disclosed, and supplier power is moderate because ten suppliers provided about 67% of purchases, though alternatives exist and the issuer states it does not expect a near-term severe impact.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: PEST factors do not appear to be a primary credit driver based on the provided materials. Climate regulation of emissions and the growth of electric alternatives are stated risks that could cut propane demand or add cost over the medium term, but the filings give no quantified effect within the 12 to 24 month horizon of this review.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strengths are scale, tank-owning customers, resilient adjusted margins, a completed refinancing with restored ratings, and cash-paid preferred units. The weaknesses are weather dependence, thin free cash flow after fixed claims, a higher coupon and rising preferred rate, maturities concentrated in 2028 and 2029, and control by a general partner whose payout limits are contractual.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C03; calculation C07; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 143–149

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The opportunities that could improve credit quality are management's weather-agnostic growth, the 6,100 conversions of Will Call locations to automatic fill, tank exchange location growth of 3.83% and the right to redeem the 2031 notes at fixed prices after January 2028. The threats that could weaken it are a warm winter, a failed or costly refinancing of the revolver and the 2029 notes, and the forced-sale path open to preferred holders from March 2031.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Scale and market position are strong: a second-largest US retail position and a national tank exchange network. Competitive advantage is average, since tank ownership and national scale help but propane is a commodity with local rivals. Business diversification is average, with many customer types and all states served but one fuel and one weather risk. Cost and capex flexibility is average, with a large fixed share of cost and a 36.22% maintenance share of capital expenditure. Margin stability is average, leaning strong on the issuer's adjusted basis, with adjusted margin between 17.06% and 17.28% in three years.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C01; calculation C10; calculation C15; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 14–16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Free cash flow stability is weak, with conversion of 23.45% after 17.04% and 55.05%. The ability to refinance and access capital markets is average, since the 2025 refinancing and the rating upgrades show access but at a coupon 387.5 bp higher and with 58.27% of principal due in a six-month window. Liquidity position is average, with USD 195.1 million at year end but a fall of USD 64.6 million and seasonal use of a facility whose borrowing base is not detailed. Financial policy and governance is average, in line with a medium governance risk level.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C03; calculation C06; calculation C07; calculation C08; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main credit supports are scale, stable margins and a completed refinancing; the constraints are free cash flow, rising fixed charges and concentrated maturities; the trend in cover and conversion is down since fiscal 2024; and the missing datapoints are the covenant definitions, the borrowing base detail and any forecast.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next 12 to 24 months the revolver is the pivotal event: it matures on October 27, 2028, within about two years, while the 2029 notes mature in April 2029, so extension or replacement of the revolver is due inside the review horizon. The preferred distribution rate steps up in March 2027 and March 2028, which adds to fixed claims ahead of equity, and the credit agreement payout condition tightens to 5.00x from the quarter ending April 30, 2027. Winter weather decides fiscal 2027 earnings, and the issuer states it believes cash flow, cash and the revolver are sufficient for the foreseeable future, which is management language.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C12; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 143–146; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 149–150; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 64–65

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over three to five years the 2029 notes, the 2031 notes in January 2031 and the preferred investor right in March 2031 fall in sequence, so access to capital markets at rating levels near B decides the outcome. Tailwinds are weather normalisation, tank exchange growth of 3.83% in selling locations and management's conversions of Will Call locations; headwinds are warm winters, labour and fuel cost, rising preferred distribution cost and any decline in propane demand from climate policy or electrification. Each tailwind is supported by a stated figure, but none is shown to change cover materially.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C02; calculation C07; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 62–63; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 145–148

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The operating event is a winter as warm as fiscal 2026 or warmer, hitting the second and third quarters. Volume falls about as in fiscal 2026, revenue follows, and because most operating cost is personnel and delivery assets, adjusted EBITDA falls by about as much as the 2.84% of fiscal 2026 or more. Interest and preferred distributions do not fall, so cover moves down from 2.54x, free cash flow after preferred distributions approaches zero, and the revolver is drawn above the USD 87.5 million of year end, which also pushes up the cash interest on variable-rate borrowings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C01; calculation C03; calculation C05; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 62–63

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Receivables and inventory fall with volume, so the borrowing base shrinks as the revolver is used, and liquidity declines from USD 195.1 million toward the floors in the payout tests. The first observable break is cash interest cover on the cash-paid basis, followed by revolver use in the summer trough, and then the refinancing of the revolver in 2027 or 2028 at a time of low cover, with the 2029 notes next. Management levers are deferring non-maintenance capital expenditure, withholding payouts and extending the revolver early, but none is shown to be sufficient on its own.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C06; calculation C07; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 143–145; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 152

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress through one warm winter, because adjusted EBITDA fell only 2.84% in fiscal 2026 and no senior notes mature before April 2029, but it is not shown to be sufficient for a second consecutive warm winter combined with the 2028 and 2029 refinancing. Default is not assumed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C01; calculation C07; 10-K_2026-07-31_fgpr-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 143–147

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Ferrellgas presents an adequate business profile supported by scale, tank-owning customers and resilient adjusted margins, but credit quality is constrained by thin free cash flow after cash interest and preferred distributions, a higher coupon and rising preferred rate, and maturities concentrated between October 2028 and April 2029. Cash-flow durability appears adequate for debt service in a normal winter and weak for deleveraging, because free cash flow converted 23.45% of adjusted EBITDA and preferred payouts took 87.24% of it. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on cover at the time of the 2028 revolver renewal, on the borrowing base and on the rating agencies' view after the October 2025 upgrades. The primary downside path is a warm winter that cuts volume while interest and preferred claims continue. A comparison with typical leveraged-credit issuers in the sector is not established because no peer data was supplied. Further analysis would require the executed debt documents and covenant ratios, the borrowing base detail, quarterly cash flows and a forecast.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C02; calculation C03; calculation C07; Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit analysis completed. Top risk: a warm winter that lowers cash interest cover before the 2028 revolver and 2029 note refinancing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: All amounts are USD; statements are in thousands and money tables in US$m with three decimals (thousands divided by 1000). Displayed percentages and ratios are rounded to two decimals half up. Gallons are in thousands as printed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Material: The executed credit agreement and indentures, and the issuer's own covenant ratios, are not supplied.
